note: Rabobank's page for its Rabo GoldCard: with a Rabo Standaard package the first card costs 2.00 euros a month, and the month's card spending is taken from the current account in full between the 24th and the 28th of the next month, so nothing is carried on it. The main banks: ING, Rabobank and ABN AMRO, the Netherlands' three largest. On 2026-10-30 ING's site didn't answer an automated request and Rabobank's refused one (403), so the Rabo GoldCard read on 2026-10-29 is kept as it was and no ING card is written. ABN AMRO's credit card pages (read 2026-10-30): the ABN AMRO Credit Card (2.55 euros a month), Gold Card (4.45 euros a month; the overview gives the figure and the card's own page says it's charged by the month) and Studenten Creditcard (1.31 euros a month; for students, not checked), each card account collected from the current account automatically every month, so nothing is carried on them. Its rates page for everyday banking (read 2026-10-30) confirms the Credit Card's and Gold Card's monthly prices; none of the pages gives a cash, foreign currency or default fee for the cards. ICS (International Card Services, of the ABN AMRO group), the Netherlands' largest card issuer, which issues cards under its own name and for other banks, was added in wave 4 as the third issuer because ING's site didn't answer: its Visa and Mastercard comparison pages and its page on how a credit card works, read 2026-10-30. The Visa World Card Platinum (175 euros a year), World Card Gold (59.50), World Card and World Card Panda (42.95 each), and the Mastercard Black (225), Gold (46.50) and Classic (38.95); every month all the card's spending is paid back at once, so nothing is carried; a cash withdrawal inside or outside the EU costs 4%. Interest at the statutory rate is charged on arrears of two months or more, which varies and isn't written; the pages give no foreign-currency surcharge for these cards. SNS Bank's credit card, which ICS also issues, costs 37.50 euros a year with 4% on cash and a 2% exchange surcharge (its cost page, read 2026-10-30), but its pages don't say how the balance is settled, so it isn't written.
